audit.why: Early lane favors Mel (Azir soldier-less pre-3), inverts at first item; content layer and packet chart both say so.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[5] and phases[6] whys describe Mel winning while packet chart and content win[] give those stages to Azir.
audit.why: Azir's first-item (Nashor's/Blackfire) soldier DPS out-ranges Mel's poke; late Azir with R is a premier teamfight mid.
audit.corrected: Rows 5-6 flipped to Azir with matching whys and ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Azir's Shifting Sands (E) shield absorbing Mel's burst was never stated; breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers.
audit.why: E is a 22s (rank 1) shield-dash — the decisive commit-timing interaction. Soldier attacks are projectile attacks Mel's W can answer; E dash and R wall are not projectiles.
audit.corrected: E shield + 22s cooldown folded into dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns; projectile distinction stated in dontsFull[2].d.

audit.why: Kit gives E 22s, R 120s, Mel W 38s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Do's/Don'ts bullets were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad pastes.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His Nashor's/Blackfire spike: stacked soldiers out-range and out-sustain your poke. Farm, don't duel.
edits.note: row flipped to Azir; why now matches content whys[5]

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Full-stack Azir with Emperor's Divide out-scales you: reflect soldier pokes, stay out of wall range, clean up chipped bars.
edits.note: row flipped to Azir; matches content whys[6]

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands: 22s at rank 1 (16 max) — his shield-dash to a soldier. Engage only after he burns it. - Emperor's Divide is 120s; while it's down your all-in actually sticks. - Your W Rebuttal is 38s early — spent on poke it's a death you scheduled.

edits.before: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Shifting Sands shields and dashes him to a soldier — the shield eats your burst; commit after he burns it, a 22s hole.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Pre-3 he has no soldiers to answer with: auto and Q the moment he steps to a minion, and every chip banks Overwhelm stacks.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Soldier stabs are projectiles your Rebuttal answers; his E dash and the Emperor's Divide wall are not — the shove goes through the glow.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by stacking soldiers to out-range you after first item and walling your all-in with Emperor's Divide.

notes: Full-layer chart carried a blanket 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] already held Mel x5 / Azir x2 (matching the packet chart), so side edits are unpaired by design per the chart rule. Rows 5-6 whys rewritten to match the Azir verdict; rows 0-4 whys already describe Mel winning. Claim that Mel W answers Azir soldier attacks is consistent with existing page text (spikes[3]) and Wind Wall precedent; flagged Medium-High rather than re-verified on the web. suspectName 'Land Emperor's Divide' in wants.foe[1] is the AbilityName convention with a verb — real name Emperor's Divide is correct, no edit needed.
